draft.title: The muscular system
card: Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and pull on them to move the body. A muscle can only pull, not push, so muscles work in pairs.
the muscle that contracts to cause a movement. It is also called the prime mover.
the muscle that relaxes and lengthens as the agonist contracts. When the movement reverses, the two muscles swap roles.

A concentric contraction is when the muscle shortens while it produces force. An eccentric contraction is when it lengthens while it produces force. An isometric contraction is when it produces force and stays the same length, so there is no movement at the joint.
draft.remember: Muscles pull in pairs: one contracts, one relaxes. The contraction type depends on whether the muscle shortens, lengthens or stays the same length.

a.q: Lena bends her elbow to lift a cup to her mouth. The biceps is the agonist. What is the triceps doing?
opts: Relaxing and lengthening as the antagonist
Contracting and shortening as the agonist
Contracting while staying the same length
Pushing the forearm up as the antagonist
a.why: The biceps contracts to bend the elbow, so the triceps on the other side of the arm is the antagonist and relaxes. Muscles cannot push, so the idea that the triceps pushes the forearm up is wrong.
a.clue: The antagonist does the opposite job to the agonist.

b.q: Sam lowers a heavy dumbbell slowly from his shoulder, and his biceps lengthens while still producing force. What type of contraction is the biceps performing?
b.why: The biceps is producing force while it lengthens, which is an eccentric contraction. Concentric is the tempting answer because the biceps is working hard, but a concentric contraction needs the muscle to shorten.
b.clue: Look at what happens to the length of the muscle.

a.best: Relaxing and lengthening as the antagonist
